llm.summary: This is a disclosed podcast-downloader skill with some sloppy metadata and default temporary-file deletion, but no artifact-backed malicious behavior.

dimensions.detail: The documented dependencies curl, jq, and ffmpeg and the configurable output directory are proportionate for downloading, parsing, converting, and saving podcast content.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, background setup, executable payload, or persistence mechanism is present; however, SKILL.md references scripts/download.sh, reference.md, and LICENSE.txt that are absent from the package.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest includes unrelated code-generation/programming-assistance text and broad/fragmented trigger keywords, which could cause overbroad invocation, but the runtime workflow itself remains focused on podcast downloading.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The workflow deletes the downloaded m4a after conversion by default, but this is disclosed in the workflow and can be overridden with KEEP_M4A=true; no credential use, background process, or privilege escalation is shown.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is downloading Xiaoyuzhou podcast audio/show notes and converting audio to MP3; network access, shell execution, and filesystem writes are aligned with that purpose, though the referenced script files are not present in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with an agent using shell tools to download audio, run ffmpeg, and write files to a podcast directory. Review the missing referenced script before relying on it, and set KEEP_M4A=true if you want to preserve original downloads.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: The unrelated code-generation language is present and should be cleaned up, but it appears to be metadata/template pollution rather than hidden behavior or a purpose-incompatible workflow.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad trigger keywords are a real quality and invocation-scope concern, but the artifact does not instruct automatic downloads or command execution without a user-provided podcast URL.
[SQP-2] expected: Deleting the source m4a after MP3 conversion is purpose-aligned disk cleanup and is documented with an opt-out variable, though it should be more prominent in the summary/quick start.
